issues_detected.description: is_deidentified.method is 'HIPAA Safe Harbor' and regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant is 'compliant', yet the release distributes spectrograms, Mel spectrograms and MFCCs, which are invertible to audio, and the record itself states 'voice can never be fully de-identified' and 'K-anonymization at k of 2 or greater is not achieved'. Safe Harbor lists biometric identifiers among the 18 categories, so the method label sits in tension with the residual-risk statement; the record mitigates this by scoping raw audio to controlled access and removing free-speech features.
issues_detected.recommendation: State explicitly that Safe Harbor applies to the phenotype tables and that derived acoustic features are released under registered access precisely because they are not Safe Harbor de-identifiable.

issues_detected.description: collection_timeframes records the healthsheet answer that 'the data were collected over a period of twelve months', while version_access documents participants being added across releases from November 2024 (v1.0, 306 participants) to May 2026 (v3.1.0, 833 participants) and the acquisition protocol describes a four-year study. The twelve-month figure was written for an earlier release and is recorded without that scope being attached to it.
issues_detected.recommendation: Attach the twelve-month statement to the v1.0/v2.0.0 healthsheet scope or replace it with the dated collection window of the v3.1.0 release.

issues_detected.description: acquisition_methods states the protocol involves 'eleven academic sites in the United States' while description, collection_mechanisms and known_limitations state five recording sites in North America and data_collectors lists Canadian institutions (University of Toronto, Mount Sinai Hospital, Hospital for Sick Children). The protocol-level and release-level site counts are both sourced but the 'in the United States' qualifier contradicts the Canadian sites named elsewhere.
issues_detected.recommendation: Qualify the eleven-site figure as the IRB protocol's planned US footprint and the five-site figure as the released data.

issues_detected.description: Two DOIs identify the resource: id 'doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42' (latest-version DOI) and doi '10.13026/8xbn-nq66' (v3.1.0 DOI). Both carry the PhysioNet prefix 10.13026 and the record declares the distinction in source_caveats ('they are not interchangeable'). The id lacks the https://doi.org/ resolver form while citation uses it.
issues_detected.recommendation: Keep the split but normalise id to the resolvable https://doi.org/10.13026/37yb-1t42 form.

issues_detected.description: conforms_to is 'Brain Imaging Data Structure v1.9.0' and conforms_to_standard is [BIDS] for a voice/acoustic dataset. This is sourced (preprocessing_strategies: 'converted to be compliant with the Brain Imaging Data Structure v1.9.0, with a phenotype directory ... and per-participant session directories holding audio and its sidecar JSON') and BIDS has no formal audio modality, so it describes the directory layout rather than a domain data standard.
issues_detected.recommendation: State that BIDS is used as a layout convention and name the acoustic feature conventions (openSMILE eGeMAPS set, Parquet schema) as the interoperability standards.

issues_detected.description: Two entries are placed in slots whose meaning they do not match: subpopulations 'Enrollment target' (subpopulation_elements_present: false) records a sample-size target rather than a subgroup, and external_resources 'Guarantees and archival status of linked resources' records a healthsheet answer ('NA') rather than a resource.
issues_detected.recommendation: Move the enrollment target to sampling_strategies and the archival-guarantee answer to notes or future_guarantees at the dataset level.

issues_detected.description: keywords holds four generic terms ('health', 'biomarkers', 'bridge2ai', 'voice'); no term names the disease cohorts, acoustic feature types, or data formats that the description enumerates.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add cohort and modality keywords (e.g. voice disorders, Parkinson's disease, depression, respiratory, spectrogram, MFCC, PhysioNet).

issues_detected.description: publisher is absent as a field although PhysioNet is the publisher in citation ('PhysioNet. RRID:SCR_007345') and maintainers names the MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology as PhysioNet's operator.

Source conflicts are recorded rather than reconciled, correctly declared each time: enrollment target 10,000 vs 30,000; healthsheet 'No' to cleaning vs the release audit protocol; healthsheet 'no erratum' vs release-note fixes; award spelled five ways including the garbled 'Award #3Tf-OTOD03272001S2'; investigator affiliations differing between documentation and publication; 'Siu' vs 'Sui'.
issues_detected.recommendation: No change to the record; these are honest source_caveats. The project should reconcile the healthsheet with the v3.1.0 release notes.

issues_detected.description: known_biases uses free-text bias_type values (representation_bias, selection_bias, measurement_bias, sampling_bias) that read as BiasTypeEnum-style terms but carry no AIO or CROISSANT RAI mapping, and no quantitative fairness analysis is given for the stated 'skews based on disorder category, site and other demographic factors'.
issues_detected.recommendation: Map each bias_type to an AIO term and add the per-cohort and per-site counts that would make the skew measurable.

semantic_insights: DOI prefix 10.13026 (PhysioNet) is correct for both the latest-version and the v3.1.0 DOI, and per-version DOIs in version_access (10.13026/249v-w155, 10.13026/k81f-qr68, 10.13026/8xbn-nq66) and the Health Data Nexus DOI 10.57764/qb6h-em84 are consistently formed.

Grant numbers OT2OD032720, 3OT2OD032720-01S1 and 3OT2OD032720-01S3 follow the NIH OT2 core/supplement pattern; the record correctly identifies OT2OD032720 as the core project number common to all spellings.

RRID:SCR_007345 in the citation follows the RRID:SCR_ format and is the PhysioNet resource RRID, so it identifies the repository rather than the dataset, which is the standard PhysioNet citation practice.

Human-subjects logic is fully closed: involves_human_subjects: true is matched by ethical_reviews (USF Single IRB, protocol first issued 17 January 2023, thirteen revisions to 11 July 2025, HRP-416 pediatric checklist), informed_consent (three modalities, assent and guardian consent), participant_compensation (40/80 USD, cap 120 USD) and at_risk_populations.

Privacy logic is closed: is_deidentified names a method and enumerates removed identifiers; participant_privacy states the anonymization method, residual reidentification_risk, data_linkage handling and recipient-side safeguards; the controlled-access tier for raw audio is proportionate to the stated risk that 'voice can never be fully de-identified'.

Funding-purpose alignment holds: the award title 'Voice as a Biomarker of Health - Building an ethically sourced, bioaccoustic database' matches purposes 'Ethically sourced voice database for AI research' and 'Integration of voice as a biomarker in clinical care'.

Temporal ordering is consistent: award start 2022-09-01, IRB v1 17 January 2023, exploratory phase completed November 2023, compensation amendment August 2023, v1.0 on Health Data Nexus end of November 2024, PhysioNet releases 17 January 2025 through 1 May 2026, issued '2026-05-01', award end 2026-11-30.

The record disciplines scope correctly: the pediatric dataset (doi:10.13026/mf9s-5r03) is held in related_datasets with relationship_type is_supplemented_by and 'is a distinct dataset from the adult release this record describes, not a version of it', and instances.counts 833 refers to the adult release only.

Tool documentation carries a version for the primary pipeline ('The v3.1.0 release was generated with b2aiprep v3.0.0') and concrete signal-processing parameters (25 ms window, 10 ms hop, 400-point FFT, 60 Mel bins, 50 Hz articulatory traces, 100 Hz posteriorgrams).

questions.description: Version access, errata, updates, derivation, parent datasets, splits, provenance lineage
questions.score_label: Version history + textual lineage; no formal provenance graph
questions.evidence: version_access with per-version DOIs and content deltas; errata (3); updates; raw_data_sources ('Original voice recordings', 'Electronic health record extracts') and raw_sources with access_url; preprocessing_strategies giving the derivation chain raw WAV -> b2aiprep v3.0.0 standardisation -> torchaudio/SPARC/openSMILE/Praat features -> Parquet/TSV, and questionnaire data 'retrieved from ReproSchema-UI or exported from REDCap'; data_collectors as agents; missing_data_documentation with handling_strategy ('a missingness table is included'); splits 'No predefined splits'; extension_mechanism. was_derived_from and parent_datasets absent.
questions.quality_note: Entity (raw audio, EHR extracts), activity (standardisation, feature extraction, audit) and agent (b2aiprep, site teams, release team) relationships are recoverable from prose with tool versions and parameters, which exceeds the version-history-only anchor, but there is no structured derivation (was_derived_from, PROV-O) linking each released file to its source, so the top anchor is not reached.

questions.name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
questions.description: Known biases with standard taxonomy and fairness analysis
questions.score_label: Typed bias categorisation with mitigation; no AIO mapping or fairness analysis
questions.evidence: known_biases (4): 'Uneven representation of disease categories' bias_type representation_bias with mitigation_strategy; 'Recruitment through specialty clinics and trust in the medical system' selection_bias with mitigation ('partnerships with community outreach clinics'); 'Device and site confounded with diagnostic label' measurement_bias ('distinct tablet devices were used at each site'), no mitigation; 'Non-probability sampling from limited locations' sampling_bias with mitigation ('shifting to remote collection'). future_use_impacts: distributional skew. addressing_gaps: 'Creating benchmarks of diversity metrics and minimizing the risk of algorithmic bias'.
questions.quality_note: Biases are systematically typed and three of four carry mitigation, which is well beyond basic identification. No AIO/CROISSANT RAI mapping is given and no quantitative fairness analysis (per-cohort or per-site counts) supports the stated skews, so one point is withheld.

strengths: Complete, closed ethics and privacy documentation: single-IRB protocol with dates and revision count, consent modalities and assent thresholds, compensation amounts, Certificate of Confidentiality, enumerated Safe Harbor identifiers and an explicit residual re-identification risk statement.
Two-tier access governance fully specified (PhysioNet registered access; Synapse controlled access via DACO) with fees, term, IP terms, confidentiality level and accountable organisation.
Versioning and sustainability at the top anchor: per-version DOIs, errata, semi-annual cadence, retention rules and a grant-funded domain repository.
Reproducible technical documentation: b2aiprep v3.0.0, 16 kHz resampling, STFT/Mel/MFCC parameters, articulatory and posteriorgram feature specifications, per-file record counts.

Rigorous scope and source discipline: the pediatric dataset is held as a typed relation, conflicting sources are recorded with manifest-ranking rationale, and stale healthsheet statements are flagged.
weaknesses: Only four generic keywords; no cohort, modality or repository terms.
No demographic or per-cohort/per-site counts for the 833 participants despite the record stating skews on exactly those axes.
Tool versions given only for b2aiprep; openSMILE, Praat, Parselmouth, torchaudio, SPARC and Whisper are unversioned; no imputation policy.
The feasibility publication and audiomics white paper relied on in source_caveats are never formally cited; publisher field absent.

Safe Harbor label sits in tension with released invertible acoustic features and the record's own 'k-anonymity not achieved' statement; the collection timeframe carries a stale twelve-month healthsheet figure.
recommendations: Expand keywords with cohort names (Parkinson's disease, depression, laryngeal cancer, COPD), feature types (spectrogram, MFCC) and 'PhysioNet'.
Add subpopulation distributions (counts by cohort, site, age band, sex, ethnicity) to subpopulations and move 'Enrollment target' to sampling_strategies.
Record versions and URLs for every tool in used_software (openSMILE, Praat/Parselmouth, torchaudio, SPARC, Whisper Large) and state the imputation policy explicitly.
Cite the feasibility publication and audiomics white paper with DOIs in citation/external_resources and populate publisher with PhysioNet.

Scope the de-identification statement per file type (Safe Harbor for phenotype tables; registered access for acoustic features because they are not Safe Harbor de-identifiable), and attach the twelve-month collection figure to the release it describes; extend future_use_impacts with mitigation for biometric misuse of voice features and map bias_type values to AIO terms.
